verses.text: After this, Jesus travelled around in Galilee. He did not want to go about in Judea, because the Jewish leaders there were looking for a way to kill him.
But the Jewish Festival of Shelters was coming near.
So Jesus' brothers said to him, "You should leave here and go to Judea, so that your followers there can see the things you do.
No one who wants to be famous does things in secret. Since you are doing these things, show yourself to the world!"
Even his own brothers did not believe in him.
Jesus told them, "The right time for me has not yet come. But for you any time is right.
The world cannot hate you, but it hates me, because I tell it that what it does is evil.
You go up to the festival. I am not going up to this festival yet, because my time has not yet fully come."
After saying this, he stayed on in Galilee.
But after his brothers had gone up to the festival, he went up too. He did not go publicly, but in secret.
At the festival the Jewish leaders were watching for him and asking, "Where is that man?"
Many people in the crowd were whispering about him. Some said, "He is a good man." Others said, "No, he is misleading the people."
But no one would speak about him openly, because they were afraid of the Jewish leaders.
When the festival was half over, Jesus went up to the temple courts and began to teach.
The Jewish leaders were amazed and asked, "How does this man know so much when he has never been taught?"
Jesus answered, "What I teach is not my own. It comes from the one who sent me.
Anyone who chooses to do what God wants will find out whether my teaching comes from God or whether I am speaking on my own.
Whoever speaks on their own does it to win honour for themselves. But the one who works for the honour of the one who sent him is truthful. There is nothing false about him.
Did Moses not give you the law? Yet not one of you keeps the law. Why are you trying to kill me?"
The crowd answered, "You have a demon! Who is trying to kill you?"
Jesus said to them, "I did one miracle, and you are all amazed.
Moses gave you circumcision (although it really came from your ancestors, not from Moses), and so you circumcise a boy even on the Sabbath.
If a boy can be circumcised on the Sabbath so that the law of Moses is not broken, why are you angry with me for making a whole person well on the Sabbath?
Stop judging by what you see on the outside. Judge fairly and rightly."
Then some of the people of Jerusalem began to ask, "Is this not the man they are trying to kill?
Here he is, speaking openly, and they are not saying a word to him. Have the leaders really decided that he is the Christ?
But we know where this man comes from. When the Christ comes, no one will know where he comes from."

Then Jesus, who was still teaching in the temple courts, called out, "Yes, you know me, and you know where I come from. But I have not come on my own. The one who sent me is true. You do not know him,
but I know him, because I come from him and he sent me."
At this they tried to arrest him, but no one laid a hand on him, because his time had not yet come.
Still, many people in the crowd believed in him. They said, "When the Christ comes, will he do more miraculous signs than this man has done?"
The Pharisees heard the crowd whispering these things about him. So the chief priests and the Pharisees sent temple guards to arrest him.
Jesus said, "I will be with you only a little longer, and then I am going back to the one who sent me.
You will look for me, but you will not find me. You cannot come where I am going."
The Jewish leaders said to one another, "Where does this man plan to go that we cannot find him? Will he go to our people who are scattered among the Greeks, and teach the Greeks?
What does he mean when he says, 'You will look for me, but you will not find me,' and 'You cannot come where I am going'?"
On the last and greatest day of the festival, Jesus stood up and called out in a loud voice, "If anyone is thirsty, let them come to me and drink.
Whoever believes in me, as the Scriptures say, rivers of living water will flow from deep inside them."
By this he meant the Spirit, whom those who believed in him would receive later. Up to that time the Spirit had not been given, because Jesus had not yet been raised to glory.
When they heard his words, some of the people said, "This man really is the Prophet."
Others said, "He is the Christ." But others asked, "How can the Christ come from Galilee?
Do the Scriptures not say that the Christ will come from the family of David, and from Bethlehem, the town where David lived?"
So the people were divided because of Jesus.
Some wanted to arrest him, but no one laid a hand on him.
Finally the temple guards went back to the chief priests and Pharisees, who asked them, "Why did you not bring him in?"
The guards answered, "No one ever spoke the way this man does!"
"Has he fooled you too?" the Pharisees asked.
"Have any of the leaders or any of the Pharisees believed in him?
No! But this crowd, who know nothing about the law, are under a curse."
Nicodemus, the man who had gone to Jesus earlier and who was one of the Pharisees, spoke up.
He asked, "Does our law condemn a man without first hearing him to find out what he has done?"
They replied, "Are you from Galilee too? Study the Scriptures and you will see that no prophet comes out of Galilee."
Then they all went home.
